Add/Drop at Binghamton: What the Data Show

Harpur College, Spring 2026, with six terms of context

Author

Dave Clark

Published

September 14, 2026

1 The window, and how days are counted

Spring 2026 add/drop opened Thursday 15 January and closed Monday 2 February: 19 calendar days, but only 10 instructional days. Classes began Tuesday 20 January. Monday 19 January was Martin Luther King Day.

Days below are counted in instructional days, not calendar days. Weekends and MLK Day are not counted; everything before the first class meeting is pooled as “before classes.” Calendar counting would drop four near-empty days into the middle of the window.

code 
day_frame %>%
  transmute(Date = format(day, "%a %d %b"),
            `Calendar day` = period_day,
            `Instructional day` = if_else(is.na(instr_day), "--", as.character(instr_day)),
            Phase = as.character(phase)) %>%
  tbl(align = "lccl") %>%
  row_spec(which(is.na(day_frame$instr_day)), background = "#D9D9D9")

Scope. Harpur students only: 5,862 students, 33,320 Banner transaction rows. The courses are not restricted to Harpur. Graduate students are 1.7% of rows, so every graduate figure below rests on a small base.

Counting. Banner writes one row per section, so dropping a course with a lecture, a discussion, and a lab writes three rows. Those collapse into one event — one student, one course, one direction, one day — taking 33,320 rows down to 26,241 events for full-semester courses.

2 When add/drop happens

code

ggplot(daily, aes(x = day, y = n, fill = direction)) +

       title = "Two peaks: the first day of classes, and the deadline",
       subtitle = "Harpur students, full-semester courses, Spring 2026") +

           label = "Before classes", colour = "grey15", size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-02-02"), y = 1450,

code 
ggplot(cum_tab, aes(x = iday, y = share)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(.25, .5, .75), colour = "grey85", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_line(colour = bucolors$green, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(colour = bucolors$green, size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1)),
            vjust = -1.1, colour = "grey15", size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, labels = c("Before\nclasses", 1:10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(x = "Instructional day", y = "Cumulative share of events",

code 
ev %>%
  count(iday, direction) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(Total = Add + Drop,
         `Cumulative %` = round(100 * cumsum(Total) / sum(Total), 1)) %>%
  left_join(iday_labels, by = "iday") %>%
  transmute(`Instr. day` = if_else(iday == 0, "--", as.character(iday)),
            Date = label, Add, Drop, Total, `Cumulative %`) %>%
  tbl(align = "clrrrr")
  • 27% of activity happens before classes meet.
  • 64% is complete by the end of class day 3.
  • 73% is complete by the end of class day 5 (the first full week).
  • 8.5% happens on the final day alone, after nine days of declining volume.

3 Adds and drops run on different clocks

code 
ev %>%
  count(direction, iday) %>%
  group_by(direction) %>%
  arrange(iday, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(share = cumsum(n) / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = iday, y = share, colour = direction)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = dir_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, labels = c("Before\nclasses", 1:10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Instructional day", y = "Cumulative share",
       title = "Adds cluster before classes; drops come after classes begin",
       subtitle = "Cumulative share within each direction, Spring 2026") +
  theme_ad()
code 
ev %>%
  group_by(Direction = direction) %>%
  summarise(Events = n(),
            `Before classes %` = round(100 * mean(iday == 0), 1),
            `Median instr. day` = median(iday),
            `After day 5 %` = round(100 * mean(iday > 5), 1),
            `On final day %` = round(100 * mean(iday == 10), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  tbl(align = "lrrrrr")

Only 17% of drops occur before the first class meeting, against 34% of adds. The median add lands on class day 2, the median drop on class day 3.

4 A third of the traffic is section swaps

A student who drops BIOL 113 section B07 and adds section A07 the same day has changed sections, not courses. In the ledger that reads as one add and one drop.

code 
ev %>%
  count(iday, action) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = iday, y = n, fill = action)) +
  geom_col(width = .8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = action_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, labels = c("Before\nclasses", 1:10)) +
  labs(x = "Instructional day", y = "Events",
       title = "Section swaps are a steady third of daily volume",
       subtitle = paste0(format(sum(ev$action == "Section swap"), big.mark = ","),
                         " of ", format(nrow(ev), big.mark = ","),
                         " events (", round(100 * mean(ev$action == "Section swap")),
                         "%) are same-course, same-day moves")) +
  theme_ad()

5 Who is doing this

code 
plot_cum <- function(g, title, pal) {
  ev %>%
    count(grp = .data[[g]], iday) %>%
    group_by(grp) %>% arrange(iday, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(share = cumsum(n) / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = iday, y = share, colour = grp)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, labels = c("Pre", 1:10)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Instructional day", y = "Cumulative share", title = title) +
    theme_ad()
}

plot_cum("level", "By student level",
         c(Undergraduate = "#005A43", Graduate = "#6CC24A")) /
plot_cum("intl", "By immigration status",
         c(Domestic = "#005A43", International = "#6CC24A")) /
plot_cum("division", "By divisional field of the course", div_cols)
code 
summ <- function(g, label) {
  ev %>%
    group_by(Group = as.character(.data[[g]])) %>%
    summarise(Events = n(),
              `Before classes %` = round(100 * mean(iday == 0), 1),
              `Median instr. day` = median(iday),
              `After day 5 %` = round(100 * mean(iday > 5), 1),
              `Adds per drop` = round(sum(direction == "Add") / sum(direction == "Drop"), 2),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Cut = label, .before = 1)
}

bind_rows(summ("level", "Level"),
          summ("intl", "Immigration status"),
          summ("division", "Division")) %>%
  tbl(align = "llrrrrr") %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")

Level. Graduate students add roughly three courses for every one they drop, undergraduates about one and a half. Timing differs much less than direction does. The base is small: 521 graduate events from 217 students.

Immigration status. No appreciable difference in timing or in the adds-per-drop ratio. Banner’s residency field is a tuition classification rather than a clean immigration variable; the technical report tests a wider definition and gets the same answer.

Division. Small differences in timing, larger ones in direction. Arts courses show the latest adds — studio, ensemble, and performance sections fill by audition and instructor permission rather than web registration. Wellness and Activity courses (HWS, Outdoor Pursuits) have the most even add-to-drop ratio in the file.

How courses were assigned to divisions

The extract carries no student major, so divisions classify the course, by subject code. All 103 subject codes are assigned in data/lookup/subject-division.csv, with a note on each judgment call. Psychology is STEM; Art History is Arts. Edit that file and re-run to change any assignment.

6 Waitlists

code 
waitlist %>%
  summarise(`Waitlist spells` = n(),
            `Distinct students` = n_distinct(id),
            `Converted to a registration` = sum(converted_after),
            `Conversion rate` = paste0(round(100 * mean(converted_after), 1), "%"),
            `Median days to convert` = median(days_to_convert[converted_after], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = " ", values_to = "  ",
               values_transform = as.character) %>%
  tbl(align = "lr")
code 
wl_day <- waitlist %>%
  mutate(iday = replace_na(instr_day, 0L)) %>%
  group_by(iday) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), conv = mean(converted_after), .groups = "drop")

w1 <- ggplot(wl_day, aes(x = iday, y = n)) +

       title = "Most waitlist spells begin before classes meet") +

w2 <- ggplot(wl_day, aes(x = iday, y = conv)) +
  geom_line(colour = bucolors$green, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n), colour = bucolors$green) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Spells") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, labels = c("Pre", 1:10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Instructional day the student joined the waitlist",
       y = "Share converting",
       title = "Conversion falls sharply with the day the student joined") +

w1 / w2
code 
waitlist %>%
  group_by(`Joined during` = phase) %>%
  summarise(Spells = n(), Converted = sum(converted_after),
            `Conversion rate` = paste0(round(100 * mean(converted_after), 1), "%"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  tbl(align = "lrrr")
code 
wl_summ <- function(g, label) {
  waitlist %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[g]])) %>%
    group_by(Group = as.character(.data[[g]])) %>%
    summarise(Spells = n(),
              `Conversion rate` = paste0(round(100 * mean(converted_after), 1), "%"),
              `Median instr. day joined` = median(replace_na(instr_day, 0L)),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Cut = label, .before = 1) %>%
    arrange(desc(Spells))
}

bind_rows(wl_summ("level", "Level"),
          wl_summ("intl", "Immigration status"),
          wl_summ("division", "Division")) %>%
  tbl(align = "llrrr") %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
code 
waitlist %>%
  group_by(course_id, division) %>%
  summarise(Spells = n(), Converted = sum(converted_after),
            Rate = mean(converted_after), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(Spells >= 15) %>%
  arrange(Rate, desc(Spells)) %>%
  transmute(Course = course_id, Division = as.character(division), Spells, Converted,
            `Conversion rate` = paste0(round(100 * Rate, 1), "%")) %>%
  head(25) %>%
  tbl(align = "llrrr")

None of the 2,237 spells belongs to a graduate student. Wellness and Activity courses generate more waitlist demand than STEM and convert the least of it; these are small activity sections with hard caps.

One caveat on the last day. A student who joins a waitlist on 2 February has no window left in which to convert, so the final-day rate is mechanically zero. The decline starts well before that: week 1 joiners had five or more class days remaining and still converted at about half the pre-term rate.

7 Six terms of context

The eight historical exports do not capture the same transaction codes as each other, so total add/drop volume cannot be compared across terms. One series is captured consistently in six of them: student web drops, also the largest single behavior in the file.

code 
dc_cmp <- terms %>%
  filter(status == "DC", export_family == "A") %>%
  count(term, season, iday) %>%
  group_by(term) %>% arrange(iday, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(share = cumsum(n) / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()

ggplot(dc_cmp, aes(x = iday, y = share, colour = term, linetype = season)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = term_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Fall = "solid", Spring = "22"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:11, labels = c("Pre", 1:11)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Instructional day", y = "Cumulative share of the term's web drops",
       title = "Drop timing has been stable for four years",
       subtitle = "Student web drops, Harpur students, Fall 2022 through Spring 2026") +
  theme_ad()
code 
terms %>%
  filter(status == "DC", export_family == "A") %>%
  group_by(Term = droplevels(term)) %>%
  summarise(`Window (instr. days)` = max(iday),
            `Web drops` = n(),
            `Before classes %` = round(100 * mean(iday == 0), 1),
            `Median instr. day` = median(iday),
            `After day 5 %` = round(100 * mean(iday > 5), 1),
            `On final day %` = round(100 * mean(day == window_close), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  tbl(align = "lcrrrrr")

Fall and spring interleave rather than separating, so there is no seasonal difference worth preserving. Every window in the archive ran 19 to 21 calendar days and 10 or 11 instructional days — no example of a different-length window to learn from. The archive does establish that Spring 2026 is the steady state, not an unusual term.

The historical files need replacing

Spring 2026 appears in both the old export and the new workbook, which makes the gap measurable: 12,866 rows against 33,320 for the same term. The old export was selected on the date a course entered the record rather than the date of the transaction, so it omits roughly half of all drops. It carries no discussion, lab, or activity rows, and no waitlist. Six of the eight historical files record no student web registrations at all. The full audit is in the technical companion.

8 Three observations that do not depend on the unknowns

Whether a shorter window would displace activity to earlier days or suppress it cannot be settled here. Every term in the archive ran the same window length, and 8.5% of Spring 2026 activity landed on the deadline itself — a response to the deadline rather than a measure of need. Three descriptive findings do not depend on resolving that.

1. Waitlist conversion collapses over the window

58% of pre-term waitlist spells convert to a registration, falling to 31.6% in week 1 and 19.9% in week 2. Conversion after class day 5 runs at 15.3%.

2. Adds and drops are different behaviors on different schedules

Median add: class day 2. Median drop: class day 3. Only 17% of drops happen before classes meet, against 34% of adds. Drops are the later and more diffuse behavior.

3. A third of the traffic is section swaps, not enrollment change

8,272 of 26,241 events (32%) are a student moving between sections of a course they have already committed to. For an instructor’s roster this differs from students joining and leaving the course, though it is the same load on the Registrar.

9 Technical notes

code 
tibble(
  Step = c("Banner transaction rows (all parts of term)",
           "Full-semester courses only",
           "Collapsed to student x course x direction x day",
           "  of which adds", "  of which drops", "  of which same-course section swaps",
           "Distinct students"),
  N = c(nrow(sections),
        sum(sections$pot == "1"),
        nrow(ev),
        sum(ev$direction == "Add"), sum(ev$direction == "Drop"),
        sum(ev$action == "Section swap"),
        n_distinct(ev$id))
) %>% tbl(align = "lr")
  • Event date is LAST_DATE_CHANGE, when the transaction finalized. It agrees with REG_STATUS_DATE on 99.3% of rows. SECTION_ADD_DATE records original registration and is not a transaction date.
  • Waitlist entries count as adds in the headline series, since joining a waitlist is an attempt to add. Removing them shifts the day-5 completion share from 73.3% to 71.9%.
  • Mini-term and module courses (2.6% of events) are excluded; they run their own calendars.
  • Everything rebuilds from the raw workbook with Rscript R/01-build-events.R and Rscript R/02-build-terms.R. Both assert that no transaction code is unclassified, that every date falls inside the official window, and that every subject code appears in the divisional crosswalk.
